newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng Index tumbles in early trade.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng Index tumbles in early trade.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index slid at the opening on Friday, falling 193 points, or 1.5 percent, to 12,723 after fears of higher interest rates sent U.S. stocks and bonds tumbling overnight.
The index fell further, touching a low of 12,630.15, before rebounding to trade 250 down at 12,669.
"We are pretty much the tail on the end of the dog," said Janet Gillies, sales director at OCBC Securities. "But the bears have come out and sold, so this could turn around pretty fast."
The Hang Seng Index closed 202.04 points lower at 12,917.09 on Thursday on heavy turnover of more than HK$10 billion.
The loss was compounded with a fall in the Hang Seng London Reference Index overnight. The HSLR plummeted 124.32 points to close at 12,792.77. This was prompted by weakness on Wall Street.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 160.48 points to 6,878.89, and the 30-year long bond closed Thursday trading in New York 30/32 lower at 95-26/32 to yield 6.96 percent, the highest level in nearly six months.
The vulnerability of the U.S. market, which continued to hit new highs after Hong Kong began a healthy consolidation, was the chief factor dragging the market down, said Gillies.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings fell HK$3.00 to HK$188.00 on heavy turnover of HK$357.44 million and Sun Hung Kai Properties slipped HK$2.50 to HK$82.50.
Hang Seng Index futures led the market down from the open. After 40 minutes of trade, the March contract was 240 points lower at 12,610, after touching a low of 12,560 earlier in the morning.
Trading activity picked up sharply after the open with more than 4,000 contracts traded.
"There looks to be good support at 12,600," said Alistair Candlish, head of derivatives trading at W.I. Carr.
Technical analysts said the index's major saupport was at 12,600, although some saw a break to as low as 12,270.
